questions.question: Research shows that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially deadly ones. Research shows that about 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When another motorcycle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left side of your lane.
Ride in the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This stops the other rider from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause your motorcycle to wobble?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear brake locks on a dry surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: A motorcycle windshield:

options.text: Will not protect your eyes from wind.
Will protect you from objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlebar grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handlebar grip on the side you want to go. To turn left, push the left grip, then push the right to straighten up. To turn right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can use more front brake.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, your front wheel gets more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: Which is NOT an advantage of riding in a tight group?

options.text: The group takes up less space on the road.
The group is easy to see.
A tight group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tight group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding close together is better than spreading out because the group uses less space, is easier to see, and stays together at traffic lights and while passing.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when exiting a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time while riding in a group. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left side
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane before passing. This helps you see oncoming traffic better and makes other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see better.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop than normal. Also increase it on slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcycles at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcycles, except when it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are better.
Adds grip for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcycles, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. On dry roads, this area has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When you accelerate, a sidecar attached to your motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is speeding up faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the side of your motorcycle. Because of its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid wind blasts, stay out of blind spots, and avoid road hazards. It should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be:
questions.correctAnswerText: A speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that tell drivers the rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow these rules.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they may seem to be:

options.text: Going faster than they actually are.
Going slower than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may appear to be traveling faster than they really are.

questions.question: Swerving on a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of grip.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of grip to do safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver is following too closely to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in a parked car's driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. If a driver is following too closely, they may want to pass and could cut in front of you. Use your horn near parked cars with drivers inside, or near pedestrians and cyclists in the street.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can make the motorcycle hard to control.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently when carrying a passenger due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust the brake light position.

questions.question: If the road requires a longer stopping distance than normal, what should you do?

options.text: Ask someone else to ride the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Do this on slippery pavement, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Keep at least a three-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in groups communicate. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it means the group should ride in a single line.

questions.question: What is true about face shields and goggles?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratched and brittle over time and need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable material so they break away in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratched and brittle over time and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They develop scratches and become brittle as time passes. Replace them regularly to keep your eyes protected and stay comfortable.
